nodes.name: On Telegram Event
nodes.notes: Native push trigger — telegram calls this workflow the moment the event happens (no polling). Credential: Telegram bot token. Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).

nodes.name: Normalize Email Payload
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming email records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Detect Sentiment
nodes.notes: Scores the text's sentiment; ports fire positive / neutral / negative. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Groq Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: llama-3.3-70b-versatile). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: Groq API key. console.groq.com → API Keys.

nodes.name: Escalate Negative — Telegram
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Log Neutral Feedback
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Email Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Thank the Sender
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Collect All Outcomes
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Sort Emails Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty from
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Summarize documents: Telegram & Slack

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers drip-campaigns work end to end across Telegram, Slack and Google Sheets.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. On Telegram Event
2. Normalize Email Payload
3. Detect Sentiment
4. Groq Chat Model
5. Escalate Negative — Telegram
6. Log Neutral Feedback
7. Thank the Sender
8. Collect All Outcomes
9. Cap Batch Volume
10. Tag Pipeline Metadata
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Sort Emails Newest First
13. Guard Non-Empty from
14. Save Execution Metadata
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
17. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing drip-campaigns work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On Telegram Event → Normalize Email Payload → Detect Sentiment → Groq Chat Model → Escalate Negative — Telegram → Log Neutral Feedback → Thank the Sender → Collect All Outcomes → Cap Batch Volume → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Sort Emails Newest First → Guard Non-Empty from → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Telegram and Slack aligned by hand for drip campaigns
- Pushing drip-campaigns events into Telegram and Slack the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Drip campaigns work where "Normalize Email Payload" is still a manual step before Telegram
- Drip campaigns work that only reaches Telegram when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Telegram and Slack in step for drip campaigns, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Telegram or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this drip-campaigns build
- Branches rejoin before Telegram, so a drip-campaigns run reports once rather than 19 times
- Every drip-campaigns run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Telegram
- Fans the same result out to Google Sheets in the same run, for drip campaigns

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Groq API key; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

A three-way branch on sentiment, not a single IF, because 'neutral' deserves different handling than 'negative' — quietly logging positive feedback while paging a human only for genuine complaints keeps the alert channel's signal-to-noise ratio high for whoever is on the other end.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a logging step to the neutral branch too and compare its volume against the negative branch.
2. Test borderline phrases through the sentiment node to see where the positive/neutral line actually falls.
3. Add a 4th branch for a specific emotion if your sentiment provider supports finer-grained labels.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Telegram bot token**
Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).
_Gotcha:_ A bot supports only one webhook at a time — a second workflow listening on the same bot steals the updates.

**Groq API key**
console.groq.com → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Very fast and cheap, but with tight per-minute rate limits.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your drip campaigns process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

**Do not log**
drip-campaigns payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.
